options.b: Bilateral netting with each dealer in place of clearing through a central counterparty (CCP)
options.c: Free delivery of securities ahead of payment to speed up settlement
options.d: Shorter settlement cycles, central clearing, and payment-versus-payment where available

distractorExplanations.a: Longer cycles extend the exposure window between trade and settlement; T+1 shortened it to cut risk.
distractorExplanations.b: Bilateral netting leaves counterparty exposure in place; central clearing through a CCP is the stronger mitigant.
distractorExplanations.c: Free delivery before payment creates principal (Herstatt) risk; DVP and PvP tie delivery to payment.

options.a: Isolating affected systems, preserving logs, and notifying security leadership
options.b: Restoring affected systems from backup first, then reviewing logs afterward
options.c: Notifying all affected customers before isolating the compromised systems
options.d: Isolating affected systems, then waiting for FINRA approval to resume wires

distractorExplanations.b: Restoring before preserving evidence can overwrite forensic data; containment and log preservation come first.
distractorExplanations.c: Containment comes first; customer notice follows Reg S-P and state breach laws once the scope is known.
distractorExplanations.d: FINRA does not approve resumption of operations; the firm decides under its incident response and BCP plans.

series-99-readiness-check-risk-025.explanation: Incident response contains damage and supports forensic review and regulatory reporting. Each step follows the firm's incident response playbook.

options.a: Decide which individual complaints are reportable under Rule 4530
options.b: Identify systemic process failures and prioritize control improvements
options.c: Calculate restitution owed to each complainant on a case-by-case basis
options.d: Rank staff for incentive pay based on complaints logged per employee

distractorExplanations.a: 4530 reportability is decided complaint by complaint; trending looks for repeated root causes across many complaints.
distractorExplanations.c: Restitution is an individual remedy; trend analysis is for spotting systemic control weaknesses.
distractorExplanations.d: Paying by complaint counts discourages logging complaints; trending is for finding process failures.

options.a: Liability only if the customer submits a written complaint first
options.b: A Reg SHO close-out obligation by the open of trading on T+2
options.c: Financial exposure, customer harm, and regulatory conduct issues
options.d: A trade reporting break to be corrected at month-end reconciliation

distractorExplanations.a: The duty to correct and make the customer whole exists whether or not the customer complains.
distractorExplanations.b: Reg SHO close-outs address short-sale fails to deliver, not unfilled customer limit orders.
distractorExplanations.d: The issue is execution quality and customer harm, which require prompt correction rather than month-end cleanup.

series-99-readiness-check-risk-027.explanation: Mishandled orders can breach duty of care; firms must fix and compensate where appropriate. These issues require prompt correction.

options.a: Revenue per registered representative and new account openings
options.b: Net capital ratio and the size of the proprietary inventory
options.c: Average client portfolio return versus the stated benchmark
options.d: Rate of trade breaks, fail rates, or aged unreconciled items

distractorExplanations.a: Revenue and account growth are business metrics, not indicators of operational control risk.
distractorExplanations.b: Net capital and inventory size measure financial and market risk, not operational process health.
distractorExplanations.c: Portfolio performance measures investment results, not operational failure rates.

options.a: Due diligence, contract SLAs, SOC reports, and exit/contingency planning
options.b: Reliance on the vendor's SOC 2 report in place of the firm's own oversight
options.c: An indemnity clause that transfers regulatory liability to the vendor
options.d: Due diligence at onboarding, with contract reviews every five years

distractorExplanations.b: A SOC report informs oversight, but FINRA Notice 21-29 keeps supervisory responsibility with the firm.
distractorExplanations.c: Contracts cannot transfer a member firm's regulatory obligations for outsourced functions.
distractorExplanations.d: Vendor oversight must be ongoing and risk-based, not a one-time check revisited every five years.

options.a: Notify the customer that a SAR was filed once 30 days have passed
options.b: Not tip off the subject that a SAR was filed, per BSA confidentiality rules
options.c: Disclose the SAR to the customer's attorney once a written request is received
options.d: Close the account and tell the customer the SAR was the reason

distractorExplanations.a: SAR confidentiality has no time limit; disclosing a SAR to its subject is prohibited at any point.
distractorExplanations.c: SAR confidentiality bars disclosure to the subject or their counsel; regulators and law enforcement may receive it.
distractorExplanations.d: Explaining a closure by reference to a SAR is tipping off; firms may close accounts but cannot reveal the filing.
